task: Verify and report WHATSAPP_CONNECTION_METHOD transport configuration
summary: Optional WhatsApp transport selection (Claude Code, session 2329cbf3). Added WHATSAPP_CONNECTION_METHOD env setting (zod enum 'qr' | 'meta', default 'qr'; a blank value is treated as the default) in src/config/env.ts. Production credential validation is now split: OPENROUTER_API_KEY stays required whenever NODE_ENV=production (PRODUCTION_REQUIRED_KEYS); the four Meta Cloud API keys (WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN, WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID, WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN, META_APP_SECRET; exported as META_CLOUD_API_REQUIRED_KEYS) are required ONLY when NODE_ENV=production AND WHATSAPP_CONNECTION_METHOD=meta. env exposes whatsappConnectionMethod and usesMetaCloudApi. src/index.ts production boot log now names the selected transport. secretStore.ts: comment only (OVERRIDABLE_KEYS unchanged, Meta keys remain dashboard-overridable in both modes). .env.example documents the new setting and marks Meta keys as meta-mode-only; README env table + section 5 note updated. tests/unit/config/env.test.ts rewritten around the two transports (23 cases). NOT changed: QR/Baileys lifecycle (qrConnection.ts), LID handling, replyTransport, webhook router mounting, Meta Graph client, dashboard, menus, offers, requests, DB/migrations, any other test. Runtime behaviour is unchanged apart from env validation: the webhook router is still always mounted and the QR socket still resumes only when a saved session exists. Port 3005 untouched; no server was started or restarted.
reason: Production deployments on the QR/Baileys transport refused to boot because env.ts demanded all Meta Cloud API credentials whenever NODE_ENV=production, even though the QR transport never uses them. User required: QR default and credential-free in production, Meta Cloud API kept as an optional alternative whose credentials are validated only when selected, OpenRouter key still required, smallest possible change, nothing else redesigned.
